newsitem.title: POLAND: CU launches three new funds in Poland.
newsitem.headline: CU launches three new funds in Poland.

text.p: The Polish life insurance unit of Britain's Commercial Union Plc, Towarzystwo Ubezpieczen na Zycie Polska SA, launched three new investment funds on Tuesday, the deputy president of the Polish firm said.

Jaroslaw Myjak told a news conference the creation of the funds would let the firm, which currently runs only one fund, offer its customers a choice of different profits and risks when buying their insurance.
"We want to offer our clients four investment funds to let them decide in which fund they want their money to be invested," he said.
He said the company was launching a "Strategic fund", the portfolio of which would consist mainly of treasuries with only a small percentage in shares.
The "Active fund" will have some 20-50 percent in shares with the rest in treasuries, real estate, bank deposits and other instruments.

The "International fund" would invest about 40 percent of its funds on foreign markets such as the United States, western Europe, Japan and the Far East. The fund will also invest in Polish shares, bonds, commercial papers and bank deposits.
Currently Commercial Union in Poland has one fund, with a portfolio dominated by bonds, treasury bills and bank deposits.
